abstract:
Multimodal drug-target affinity (DTA) models can incorporate molecular, protein, assay and textual evidence whose availability and reliability vary under missing modalities, cold-start entities and assay distribution shift.
We present MIRAGE-DTA, a reliability-oriented evidence-arbitration layer that complements DTA encoders by keeping current-sample and training-set retrieval evidence as two explicit chains, carrying modality masks into fusion, retrieving training-only neighbors, and resolving disagreement with an interaction gate and validation-selected anchor. Across BindingDB_Kd, DAVIS, KIBA and a 2010-2024 CHEMBL_ASSAY benchmark with 35,238 interactions, experiments tested cold-start, missing-modality and assay/temporal shift settings. Under 35% sequence/text missingness on CHEMBL_ASSAY, 10-seed paired evaluation showed that MIRAGE-DTA reduced expected calibration error relative to late fusion by 0.0524, 0.0923 and 0.1018 on assay-cold, target-cold and temporal splits. Risk at 80% coverage was significantly lower on target-cold and temporal splits and numerically lower on assay-cold. A complementary complete-evidence direct-pChEMBL regression analysis also showed lower RMSE for the two-branch model than for current-only and retrieval-only regressors across assay-cold, target-cold and temporal splits. Ranking remained broadly competitive, with a modest trade-off on the temporal split, indicating that the principal benefit lies in calibrated and selective prediction under incomplete or shifted evidence. Shortcut audits quantified neighbor-overlap effects and showed that temporal retrieval was not driven by repeated compounds or near-duplicate scaffolds.
Source code is available at https://github.com/wushen1103-collab/mirage_drug_miniprototype and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22695984; data come from public sources.
